There’s a world of difference between user-authorized agents (Muse, Instinct, Grokbot, etc.) and true unauthorized/rogue agents that could constitute cyberattacks. Most of the activity described in the Axios story appears to be the former: customers sharing credentials with agents so they can take actions on their behalf. This may violate bank terms requiring humans to log in themselves, but these are in no way cyberattacks. The direction banks should go is to support user-directed agents. For example, Amex is an authorized connection in Muse, making it easy for users to grant, limit, and revoke access. Read-only permission levels are a sensible interim step. Several banks already support or are moving toward them. Full write access (with user credentials) is a different risk category and should be approached carefully. Frightening the public by blurring the line between user-authorized agentic behavior and cyberattacks is irresponsible.

posts.title: #TrendForce notes that #Micron plans to begin mass producing its 1-delta nm process in 2027, which is set to succeed its current mainstream 1-gamma nm process. Beyond this transition, Micron intends to continue scaling its 6F² architecture before moving directly to 3D DRAM, bypassing the intermediate 4F² architecture. In contrast, South Korean and Chinese DRAM manufacturers still plan to adopt 4F² architecture, highlighting a growing divergence in process technology roadmaps among major suppliers. Micron is also developing memory solutions optimized for AI solutions, including #vHBM and #vEIM, to compete with SK hynix's 3D HBM and Samsung's zHBM. In #NAND Flash, Micron is preparing to ramp up production of its G11 generation in 2H27. By incorporating wafer bonding and stacking more than 400 layers, G11 is expected to deliver twice the bit density of G9, alongside a targeted 1.5-fold improvement in I/O speed. #TrendForce believes these advances will enable Micron to close the technology gap with #Kioxia and #YMTC—both early adopters of hybrid bonding architectures—and strenghten its competitive position as NAND performance becomes increasingly critical to an AI-driven market.

身价千亿的泡泡玛特创始人王宁，提出过一个很牛逼的观点，这也是未来五年众多高利润行业的核心逻辑。 他举了这样一个例子： 千万富翁出门忘记关掉家里水龙头，一天浪费30元水费，依旧会觉得心疼。 这笔钱数额不大，但内心会觉得别扭。 可小区里的景观喷泉全天开启，每日成本至少300元，却没有任何人觉得可惜。 背后的原因很简单：水龙头对应的是实用价值，人们对实用类的成本十分敏感，习惯反复计算得失。 而喷泉提供的是情绪价值，视觉上赏心悦目，让人觉得舒心，大家便不会去核算它的成本。 由此得出结论：情绪价值，远比实用价值更值钱。 什么是情绪价值？可以看一个带货案例。 这是学员优化前的香水带货视频：一瓶5升装香水，售价三十多元，可以使用半年，是大牌同款香型。 整段话术只突出性价比、耐用度，全部都是产品参数。 观众听完心里只会产生疑问：三十多块的产品，品质能靠谱吗？ 优化之后的带货文案完全换了思路：这款香水我喷过一次，约会时对方直接乱了分寸，目光一直落在我身上，连说话的语气都变得温柔。 调整后的视频发布一周，卖出五千多单，单条视频佣金，超过他过去一整年的收入。 同样一款香水，前后效果差距巨大。 优化前，反复强调低价、大容量、大牌平替，句句都是产品实用参数。 商家以为是为消费者着想，可用户会不断权衡、犹豫，可选择的替代品也很多。 优化后的版本，全程不提价格、不讲成分，只描绘场景与感受。 喷上它去约会，会自带吸引力，让人心生好感。 用户脑海里会直接浮现画面，被情绪带动，直接下单。 我们卖给用户的，从来不是一瓶香水，而是约会时自带吸引力的底气。 讲产品参数，用户就会开始比价算账，传递情绪价值，才会促使用户当下买单。 两套话术的差距，不在于香水配方，而在于能不能给用户传递情绪感受。 参数只会让人精打细算，情绪才能驱动消费。 未来五年，谁能把情绪价值融入生意，谁就能赚到更多收益。 看懂这条逻辑的人，已经开始优化自己的产品话术了。
